correctness.rationale: For p>=5, Jacobsthal--Ljunggren lifting gives B_j=B_{j-1} modulo p^(3j), hence a p-adic limit beta with B_r=beta modulo p^r. Fermat plus LTE gives q^(p^r)=omega_p(q) modulo p^r. The original congruence is therefore exactly beta=omega modulo p^r. The low-layer equivalences use B_1=q modulo p^3 and the valuation identity v_p((q/omega)^(p-1)-1)=v_p(q/omega-1). A packaged direct replay checks 60 finite cases and 30 lifting increments without being used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source problem already isolates prime powers through its square/Wieferich theorem. Determining the entire exponent tower is a natural structural gap: the result proves the solution exponents are an initial segment, recovers squares, identifies cubes with order-three Wieferich congruences, and explains why higher layers require a new p-adic binomial invariant. This is not a parameter substitution or table extension.
